claim: Signaling via the NFκB-inducing kinase (NIK) is essential for the formation of a fully functional γδ T cell compartment.
source: Here we show that signaling via the NFκB-inducing kinase (NIK) is essential for the formation of a fully functional γδ T cell compartment.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract, supported by multiple experimental results throughout the manuscript including data from NIK-deficient mice.

claim: In the absence of NIK, development of Vγ5+ dendritic epidermal T cells (DETCs) was halted in the embryonic thymus.
source: In the absence of NIK, development of Vγ5+ dendritic epidermal T cells (DETCs) was halted in the embryonic thymus
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B,C demonstrating virtually absent DETCs in NIK-deficient embryos.

claim: Impaired NIK function caused a selective loss of IL-17 expression by γδ T cells.
source: impaired NIK function caused a selective loss of IL-17 expression by γδ T cells
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2 showing reduced IL-17 production in NIK-deficient γδ T cells.

claim: NIK signaling in thymic epithelial cells is essential for the thymic hardwiring of γδ T cell cytokine production.
source: we could show in vivo that NIK signaling in thymic epithelial cells is essential for the thymic hardwiring of γδ T cell cytokine production
evidence: This is demonstrated using conditional NIK mutants with TEC-specific deletion (Foxn1-Cre and Ccl19-Cre) shown in Figure 5.

claim: γδ T cells contribute to first line immune defense through their ability for rapid production of proinflammatory cytokines.
source: γδ T cells contribute to first line immune defense, particularly through their ability for rapid production of proinflammatory cytokines.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract drawing on established scientific knowledge about γδ T cell function.

claim: The cytokine profile of γδ T cells is hard-wired already during thymic development.
source: The cytokine profile of γδ T cells is hard-wired already during thymic development.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: γδ T cells are important players during protective immune reactions.
source: it became evident that γδ T cells are important players not only during protective immune reactions (Lockhart et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lockhart et al., 2006.

claim: γδ T cells are important players in various models of autoimmune disease.
source: it became evident that γδ T cells are important players not only during protective immune reactions (Lockhart et al., 2006), but also in various models of autoimmune disease (Petermann et al., 2010; Cai et al., 2011; Pantelyushin et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Petermann et al., 2010; Cai et al., 2011; Pantelyushin et al., 2012.

claim: γδ T cells recognize qualitatively different antigens compared to αβ T cells.
source: Most notably, γδ T cells recognize qualitatively different antigens.
evidence: This is stated as a distinguishing feature and is supported by subsequent citations about antigen recognition.

claim: Known targets of γδ T cells include non-classical MHC molecules.
source: known targets include non-classical MHC molecules (Strid et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Strid et al., 2008.

claim: Known targets of γδ T cells include phosphoantigens.
source: known targets include non-classical MHC molecules (Strid et al., 2008), phosophoantigens (Constant et al., 1994)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Constant et al., 1994.

claim: Known targets of γδ T cells include a discrete set of non-self proteins.
source: known targets include non-classical MHC molecules (Strid et al., 2008), phosophoantigens (Constant et al., 1994) as well as a discrete set of non-self proteins (Zeng et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zeng et al., 2012.

claim: γδ T cells have the ability for rapid production of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IFN-γ and IL-17 independent of TCR engagement.
source: The second main characteristic of γδ T cells is their ability for rapid production of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as INF-γ and IL-17 independent of TCR engagement (Sutton et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sutton et al., 2009.

claim: The rapid cytokine production feature of γδ T cells has been suggested to be hardwired in developing γδ T cells already during thymic development, probably in dependency of self-antigen recognition.
source: This feature has been suggested to be hardwired in developing γδ T cells already during thymic development, probably in dependency of self-antigen recognition (Jensen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jensen et al., 2008.

claim: The surface molecule CD27 distinguishes IFN-γ-producing from IL-17-producing γδ T cells.
source: The surface molecule CD27, which belongs to the tumor necrosis (TNF) receptor superfamily has been shown to distinguish IFN-γ-producing from IL-17-producing γδ T cells (Ribot et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ribot et al., 2009.

claim: Differential expression of the transcription factors T-bet and RORγt distinguishes IFN-γ-producing from IL-17-producing γδ T cells.
source: as does the differential expression of the transcription factors T-bet and RORγt and certain chemokine receptors such as CCR6 (Haas et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Haas et al., 2009.

claim: Differential expression of certain chemokine receptors such as CCR6 distinguishes IFN-γ-producing from IL-17-producing γδ T cells.
source: as does the differential expression of the transcription factors T-bet and RORγt and certain chemokine receptors such as CCR6 (Haas et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Haas et al., 2009.

claim: γδ T cells show a remarkable limitation in their TCR variability despite the theoretical genetic diversity of the TCR γδ locus.
source: Although the genetic diversity of the TCR γδ locus would theoretically allow an even higher number of different TCR specificities than for αβ T cells (Bonneville et al., 2010), γδ T cells show a remarkable limitation in their TCR variability.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with citation to Bonneville et al., 2010 for the theoretical diversity.

claim: γδ T cells with a given TCR specificity often home to non-lymphoid organs.
source: Moreover, γδ T cells with a given TCR specificity often home to non-lymphoid organs, where the majority of mature γδ T cells can be found.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about γδ T cell biology.

claim: Dendritic epidermal T cells (DETCs) are found in the murine epidermis and almost exclusively express a clonotypic TCR consisting of the Vγ5 and Vδ1 chains.
source: The prime example of tissue homing-behavior is observed in dendritic epidermal T cells (DETCs), which are found in the murine epidermis and almost exclusively express a clonotypic TCR consisting of the Vγ5 and Vδ1 chains (Asarnow et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Asarnow et al., 1988.

claim: Vγ5+ DETCs are among the very first T cells to develop during embryogenesis, populating the epidermis already around day 15/16 of fetal development.
source: Vγ5+ DETCs are among the very first T cells to develop during embryogenesis, populating the epidermis already around day 15/16 of fetal development (Xiong et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xiong et al., 2004.

claim: Vγ4+ γδ T cells (mostly IL-17 producers) migrate predominantly to the dermis and lung tissue.
source: Also other subsets of γδ T cells, such as Vγ4+ γδ T cells (mostly IL-17 producers), which migrate predominantly to the dermis and lung tissue
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations about their developmental timing.

claim: Vγ4+ γδ T cells have been shown to develop only early in ontogeny.
source: Also other subsets of γδ T cells, such as Vγ4+ γδ T cells (mostly IL-17 producers), which migrate predominantly to the dermis and lung tissue, have been shown to develop only early in ontogeny (Allison and Havran, 1991; Haas et al., 2012; Prinz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Allison and Havran, 1991; Haas et al., 2012; Prinz et al., 2013.

claim: Skint-1 has an essential function for the development of Vγ5+ DETCs.
source: One major step forward was the identification of Skint-1 (Selection and upkeep of intraepithelial T cells-1), which has an essential function for the development of Vγ5+ DETCs (Lockhart et al., 2006; Lewis et al., 2006; Boyden et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lockhart et al., 2006; Lewis et al., 2006; Boyden et al., 2008.

claim: Skint-1 is expressed by medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs).
source: Expression of Skint-1 by medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) (Barbee et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Barbee et al., 2011.

claim: Expression of Skint-1 by mTECs leads to a signaling cascade in developing γδ thymocytes that induces the typical gene expression profile of DETCs, concomitant to their preferential homing to the skin.
source: Expression of Skint-1 by medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) (Barbee et al., 2011) leads to a signaling cascade in developing γδ thymocytes that induces the typical gene expression profile of DETCs, concomitant to their preferential homing to the skin (Turchinovich and Hayday, 2011; Vantourout and Hayday, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Turchinovich and Hayday, 2011; Vantourout and Hayday, 2013.

claim: The induction of the typical gene signature of IL-17-producing Vγ4+ γδ T cells depends on the function of the transcription factor Sox13.
source: On the other hand, the induction of the typical gene signature of IL-17-producing Vγ4+ γδ T cells depends on the function of the transcription factor Sox13 (Gray et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gray et al., 2013.

claim: Signaling pathways leading to activation of NFκB are essential for the function of various immune cell compartments.
source: It has been known for some time that signaling pathways leading to activation of NFκB are essential for the function of various immune cell compartments (reviewed in Li and Verma, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a review by Li and Verma, 2002.

claim: The classical pathway of NFκB activation is induced mainly by molecular danger signals such as LPS or certain cytokines such as TNF or IL-1β.
source: The so-called classical pathway of NFκB activation is induced mainly by molecular danger signals such as LPS or certain cytokines such as TNF or IL-1β.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about NFκB signaling pathways.

claim: Non-canonical NFκB signaling requires the NFκB-inducing kinase (NIK).
source: Non-canonical NFκB signaling, which requires the NFκB-inducing kinase (hereafter referred to as NIK, the encoding gene being Map3k14,) (Malinin et al., 1997; Yin, 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Malinin et al., 1997; Yin, 2001.

claim: Non-canonical NFκB signaling is activated by a discrete subset of TNF family members, including CD40L, Lymphotoxin (LT), BAFF and RANKL.
source: is activated by a discrete subset of TNF family members, including CD40L, Lymphotoxin (LT), BAFF (B cell activating factor) and RANKL (Receptor activator of NFκB ligand).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about non-canonical NFκB pathway activation.

claim: Signaling via the non-canonical pathway has been shown to fulfill roles in B cell survival.
source: Signaling via the non-canonical pathway has been shown to fulfill roles in B cell survival (Sen, 2006)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sen, 2006.

claim: Signaling via the non-canonical pathway has been shown to fulfill roles in activation of T cells.
source: Signaling via the non-canonical pathway has been shown to fulfill roles in B cell survival (Sen, 2006), activation of T cells (Matsumoto et al., 2002; Ribot et al., 2009)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Matsumoto et al., 2002; Ribot et al., 2009.

claim: Signaling via the non-canonical pathway has been shown to fulfill roles in maturation and function of dendritic cells (DCs).
source: maturation and function of dendritic cells (DCs) (Hofmann et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hofmann et al., 2011.

claim: Signaling via the non-canonical pathway has been shown to fulfill roles in the induction of tolerance.
source: as well as the induction of tolerance (Zhu et al., 2006; Bonneville et al., 2010)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Zhu et al., 2006; Bonneville et al., 2010.

claim: Signaling via the CD70-CD27 axis can activate NFκB p52 processing.
source: Previous work has suggested that signaling via the CD70-CD27 axis (which belongs to the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily) can activate NFκB p52 processing (Ribot et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ribot et al., 2010.

claim: LTβR signaling has been implicated in the differentiation program of bulk γδ thymocytes.
source: Also, LTβR signaling has been implicated in the differentiation program of bulk γδ thymocytes (Silva-Santos, 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Silva-Santos, 2005.

claim: The NFκB family members RelA and RelB were shown to guide the development of IL-17-producing Vγ4+ γδ T cells.
source: and the NFκB family members RelA and RelB were shown to guide the development of IL-17-producing Vγ4+ γδ T cells (Powolny-Budnicka et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Powolny-Budnicka et al., 2011.

claim: The genesis of invariant NKT cells was claimed to depend on signaling via NIK.
source: Furthermore, the genesis of invariant NKT cells was claimed to depend on signaling via NIK (Elewaut et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Elewaut et al., 2003.

claim: NIK-deficient mice showed a drastic loss of DETCs in the epidermis.
source: In line with previous studies that were using knockout models of the TNF receptor family member RANKL (Roberts et al., 2012) we found that NIK-deficient mice showed a drastic loss of DETCs in the epidermis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and comparison to previous studies (Roberts et al., 2012).

claim: In the absence of NIK most of the IL-17 production by splenic and lung-resident γδ T cells was lost.
source: Of note, in the absence of NIK most of the IL-17 production by splenic and lung-resident γδ T cells was lost
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D-H.

claim: The ability of NIK-deficient γδ T cells to express IFN-γ was not affected.
source: while their ability to express IFN-γ was not affected
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D-H.

claim: Loss of IL-17 production in NIK-deficient CD27- γδ T cells was accompanied by a loss of Rorc and Sox13 expression.
source: Mechanistically, this was accompanied by a loss of Rorc and Sox13 expression in NIK-deficient CD27- γδ T cells
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: Loss of IL-17 production in NIK-deficient CD27- γδ T cells was accompanied by increased expression of Tbet and Egr3.
source: while in turn expression of Tbet and Egr3 was increased
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: NIK signaling specifically in thymic epithelium is essential for shaping the cytokine profile of the γδ T cell compartment.
source: our data suggest that NIK signaling specifically in thymic epithelium is essential for shaping the cytokine profile of the γδ T cell compartment
evidence: This is supported by conditional deletion experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: In adult Map3k14-/- mice, only 30-50% of the γδ T cells in the epidermis express the canonical Vγ5+ TCR.
source: In line with this, we observed a disturbed pool of DETCs in the epidermis of adult Map3k14-/- mice (Yin, 2001), with only 30-–50% of the γδ T cells present expressing the canonical Vγ5+ TCR (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: DETCs were virtually absent in the skin of NIK-deficient embryos at day 19 post conception.
source: Whereas there was already a prominent population of Vγ5+ DETCs present in WT controls, DETCs were virtually absent in the skin of NIK-deficient embryos (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Vγ5+ thymocytes were present in NIK-deficient thymi at embryonic day 19, albeit at reduced numbers and with a consistent reduction in staining intensity of the TCR.
source: Indeed, these cells were present in NIK-deficient thymi, albeit at reduced numbers and with a consistent reduction in staining intensity of the TCR (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The expected upregulation of CD45RB and CD122 typical for developing DETCs was not found in Map3k14-/- embryos.
source: The expected upregulation of CD45RB and CD122, which is typical for developing DETCs was not found in Map3k14-/- embryos.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The downregulation of CD24 and CD62L which normally coincides with DETC maturation was reduced in Map3k14-/- embryos.
source: In turn, the downregulation of CD24 and CD62L which normally coincides with DETC maturation was also reduced (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The loss of NIK abrogates normal development of DETC precursors in the embryonic thymus.
source: Taken together, the loss of NIK abrogates normal development of DETC precursors in the embryonic thymus
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: In both the spleen and the lung of Map3k14-/- and aly/aly animals, the total number of γδ T cells was unchanged.
source: Both in the spleen and the lung of these mutant animals, the total number of γδ T cells as well as the frequency of the two most prominent subclasses expressing the Vγ4+ and Vγ1.1+ TCR was unchanged.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The frequency of the Vγ4+ and Vγ1.1+ TCR subclasses was unchanged in Map3k14-/- and aly/aly animals.
source: Both in the spleen and the lung of these mutant animals, the total number of γδ T cells as well as the frequency of the two most prominent subclasses expressing the Vγ4+ and Vγ1.1+ TCR was unchanged.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The distribution of the CD27+ and CD27- subsets of γδ T cells was indistinguishable between Map3k14-/- and heterozygous control animals.
source: Also, the distribution of the CD27+ and CD27- subsets of γδ T cells was indistinguishable between Map3k14-/- and heterozygous control animals (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: After in vitro stimulation of bulk peripheral lymphoid γδ T cells, their ability to express IL-17 was strongly diminished in Map3k14-/- animals.
source: However, when we assessed the primary function of γδ T cells, which is the rapid production of pro-inflammatory cytokines, we noticed that after in vitro stimulation of bulk peripheral lymphoid γδ T cells their ability to express IL-17 was strongly diminished.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: The frequency of both IFN-γ and TNF-α-producing γδ T cells was similar between Map3k14-/- and control animals.
source: In contrast, the frequency of both IFN-γ and TNF-α-producing γδ T cells was similar between Map3k14-/- and control animals (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: Lung-resident γδ T cells from NIK-deficient animals showed a reduction in the ability for IL-17 secretion accompanied by a slight increase in the frequency of IFN-γ production.
source: For lung-resident γδ T cells, which include Vγ6+ γδ T cells as one the most potent sources of IL-17, we also observed a reduction in the ability of NIK-deficient cells for IL-17 secretion, but this was accompanied by a slight increase in the frequency of IFN-γ production (Figure 2F,G).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2F,G.

claim: In the steady state dermal γδ T cell compartment, in the absence of NIK, γδ T cells were impaired in IL-17 expression.
source: Similarly, for the steady state dermal γδ T cell compartment we observed that in the absence of NIK, γδ T cells were impaired in IL-17 expression (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: In NIK-deficient CD27- γδ T cells, Rorc and Il23r were drastically reduced compared to controls.
source: While in controls, CD27- γδ T cells expressed high levels of Rorc and Il23r, the same molecules were drastically reduced in NIK-deficient CD27- γδ T cells (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Loss of Rorc and Il23r in NIK-deficient CD27- γδ T cells was accompanied by an upregulation of Tbet.
source: which was accompanied by an upregulation of Tbet
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: NIK-deficiency selectively in CD27- γδ T cells led to a loss of Sox13 and a gain of Egr3 expression.
source: While the expression level of both genes was not affected in CD27+ γδ T cells, NIK-deficiency selectively in CD27- γδ T cells led to a loss of Sox13 and a gain of Egr3 expression (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: NIK signaling is essential for RORγt expression in CD27- γδ T cells.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that NIK signaling is essential for RORγt and as well as Sox13 expression in CD27- γδ T cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the qPCR data in Figure 3B,C.

claim: NIK signaling is essential for Sox13 expression in CD27- γδ T cells.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that NIK signaling is essential for RORγt and as well as Sox13 expression in CD27- γδ T cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the qPCR data in Figure 3B,C.

claim: NIK signaling confers the full potential for production of IL-17 in CD27- γδ T cells.
source: thereby conferring their full potential for production of IL-17
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing loss of IL-17 and transcription factors.

claim: After Imiquimod treatment, NIK-deficient animals displayed a slight, but not significant reduction of back skin thickness.
source: After treatment with Aldara (containing 5% Imiquimod), NIK-deficient animals displayed a slight, but not significant reduction of back skin thickness (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by measurement data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Analysis of the dermal γδ T cell compartment after Aldara treatment revealed reduced numbers of γδ T cells in NIK-deficient animals.
source: Analysis of the dermal γδ T cell compartment not only revealed reduced numbers of γδ T cells (data not shown)
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experiment.

claim: After Aldara treatment, there was a significant reduction of both IL-17A and IL-17F expression by γδ T cells in NIK-deficient animals.
source: but also a significant reduction of both IL-17A and IL-17F expression by γδ T cells (Figure 3E)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: NIK-signaling in an inflammatory setting is essential for full IL-17 production by γδ T cells.
source: This suggests that NIK-signaling also in an inflammatory setting is essential for full IL-17 production by γδ T cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Aldara treatment experiment data.

claim: Other cell types, such as ILCs, can compensate for the functional impairment of γδ T cells during Aldara induced skin inflammation.
source: but that other cell types, such as ILCs (Pantelyushin et al., 2012) can compensate this functional impairment during Aldara induced skin inflammation
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that skin inflammation was only slightly reduced despite impaired γδ T cell function, with citation to Pantelyushin et al., 2012.

claim: Map3k14del/del mice were lacking lymph nodes.
source: Examination of the resulting Map3k14del/del mice showed that these mice were lacking lymph nodes, suggesting that the conditional construct is working as expected (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by visual inspection shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Map3k14del/del mice phenocopy the full knockout with respect to cytokine production of peripheral γδ T cells.
source: To further verify the phenotype of Map3k14del/del mice, we compared the cytokine production of peripheral γδ T cells to WT and Map3k14-/- animals, showing that Map3k14del/del mice phenocopy the full knockout (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Map3k14del/del mice phenocopy the full knockout with respect to the epidermal DETC pool.
source: The same was true for the epidermal DETC pool (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Ccl19-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox animals phenocopied the aberrant DETC development observed in germline Map3k14-/- mice, with a loss of Vγ5 expression by DETCs.
source: Ccl19-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox animals phenocopied the aberrant DETC development observed in germline Map3k14-/- mice, with a loss of Vγ5 expression by DETCs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There was variation in the penetrance of the Ccl19-Cre transgene, with some litters presenting with a phenotype, while others did not.
source: However, we observed some variation in the penetrance of the Ccl19-Cre transgene, with some litters presenting with a phenotype, while others did not
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The start of Cre expression driven by Ccl19 promotor sharply coincides with the start of DETC development in the embryo.
source: suggesting that the start of Cre expression driven by Ccl19 promotor sharply coincides with the start of DETC development in the embryo
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the variable penetrance observation.

claim: Foxn1-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox showed a strong reduction in both frequency and number of skin-resident TCRγδhigh DETCs.
source: Corroborating our findings, Foxn1-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox showed a strong reduction in both frequency and number of skin-resident TCRγδhigh DETCs (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Around 90% of CD27- γδ T cells in the lung expressed yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) in Fatemap Rorc-Cre+ R26-Stop-flox-YFP mice.
source: Analysis of Fatemap Rorc-Cre+ R26-Stop-flox-YFP mice showed that around 90% of CD27- γδ T cells in the lung expressed yellow fluorescent protein (YFP), indicating a good targeting efficiency of this cellular subset (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Lung-resident γδ T cells in Rorc-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox mice expressed IL-17 at levels comparable to wildtype controls.
source: However, lung-resident γδ T cells in Rorc-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox mice expressed IL-17 at levels comparable to wildtype controls (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: γδ T cell intrinsic signaling is dispensable for the commitment of IL-17-producing γδ T cells.
source: suggesting that γδ T cell intrinsic signaling is dispensable for the commitment of IL-17-producing γδ T cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Rorc-Cre conditional deletion experiment.

claim: Both peripheral and lung-resident γδ T cells in CD4-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox mice had ability for IL-17 production comparable to wildtype controls.
source: To exclude a potential role of NIK signaling in the CD4+ αβ thymocyte compartment (Powolny-Budnicka et al., 2011), we analyzed both peripheral and lung-resident γδ T cells in CD4-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox mice. Their ability for IL-17 production was comparable to wildtype controls (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Within the αβ thymocyte compartment NIK signaling is dispensable for IL-17 production by γδ T cells.
source: demonstrating that also within the αβ thymocyte compartment NIK signaling is dispensable
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the CD4-Cre conditional deletion experiment.

claim: γδ T cells isolated from the lung of Ccl19-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox animals did not present with any abnormalities in cytokine production.
source: While γδ T cells isolated from the lung of Ccl19-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox animals did not present with any abnormalities in cytokine production
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: γδ T cells isolated from P13 Foxn1-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox mice showed significant defects in their ability for IL-17 production both in the spleen and lung.
source: γδ T cells isolated from P13 Foxn1-Cre+ Map3k14flox/flox mice showed significant defects in their ability for IL-17 production both in the spleen and lung (Figure 5D)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5D (should be 5E based on figure).

claim: NIK signaling in thymic epithelial cells is needed for imprinting the cytokine commitment onto developing γδ T cells.
source: suggesting that indeed NIK signaling in thymic epithelial cells is needed for imprinting the cytokine commitment onto developing γδ T cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conditional deletion experiments using Foxn1-Cre.

claim: The DETC defect observed in complete NIK-knockout animals is due to the requirement for NIK signaling in thymic epithelial cells.
source: As a next step, we assessed whether the DETC defect observed in complete NIK-knockout animals is due to the requirement for NIK signaling in thymic epithelial cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis tested using conditional deletion in TECs.

claim: Ccl19-Cre mice express Cre solely in lymph node stromal cells and mature medullary thymic epithelial cells.
source: To specifically delete NIK in medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs), Map3k14flox/flox mice were crossed to Ccl19-Cre mice, which express Cre solely in lymph node stromal cells and mature medullary thymic epithelial cells (Chai et al., 2013; Onder et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chai et al., 2013; Onder et al., 2015.

claim: In Foxn1-Cre mice, Cre is under control of the Foxn1 promotor and thus active in all thymic epithelial cells (both cortical and medullary).
source: Thus, we decided to utilize an additional strain targeting the thymic epithelium, namely Foxn1-Cre mice in which Cre is under control of the Foxn1 promotor and thus active in all thymic epithelial cells (both cortical and medullary) (Gordon et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gordon et al., 2007.

claim: The development of DETCs is partially dependent on signaling via the RANK-RANKL axis.
source: Previous studies have shown that the development of DETCs is partially dependent on signaling via the RANK-RANKL axis (Roberts et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Roberts et al., 2012.

claim: NIK is downstream of RANK.
source: Given that NIK is downstream of RANK (Darnay et al., 1999)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Darnay et al., 1999.

claim: The DETC deficiency observed in newborn Map3k14-/- mice was much more pronounced than in Tnfrsf11a-/- animals.
source: one would expect a similar phenotype in Map3k14-/- animals, but the DETC deficiency that we observed in newborn Map3k14-/- mice was much more pronounced than in Tnfrsf11a-/- animals
evidence: This is a comparison of phenotypes between different knockout models.

claim: During DETC development several upstream receptors converge in their signaling to NIK, making it a key pathway during thymic DETC development.
source: suggesting that during DETC development several upstream receptors converge in their signaling to NIK, making it a key pathway during thymic DETC development
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the more severe phenotype in NIK-deficient mice compared to RANK-deficient mice.

claim: For normal function of the γδ T cell compartment, NIK signaling does not act γδ cell-intrinsically but in trans by its function in thymic epithelial cells.
source: Importantly, our data obtained using the conditional NIK-mutant strongly suggests that for normal function of the γδ T cell compartment, NIK signaling does not act γδ cell-intrinsically but in trans by its function in thymic epithelial cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conditional deletion experiments.

claim: Conditional deletion of NIK solely in thymic epithelial cells was sufficient to copy the DETC phenotype seen in complete germ-line NIK-knockout animals.
source: Conditional deletion of NIK solely in thymic epithelial cells was sufficient to copy the DETC phenotype seen in complete germ-line NIK-knockout animals.
evidence: This is supported by the Foxn1-Cre and Ccl19-Cre conditional deletion data.

claim: This is the first genetic in vivo demonstration that non-canonical NFκB signaling is not required in DETCs in a cell-intrinsic manner, but through its activity in TECs.
source: We believe this to be the first genetic in vivo demonstration that non-canonical NFκB signaling is not required in DETCs in a cell-intrinsic manner, but through its activity in TECs.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings based on the experimental results.

claim: Only the neonatal thymic microenvironment appears to have the capacity to imprint a stable cytokine profile to γδ T cells.
source: Only the neonatal thymic microenvironment appears to have the capacity to imprint a stable cytokine profile to γδ T cells
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citation.

claim: The IL-17-producing γδ T cell subsets cannot be reconstituted in adult animals by bone marrow transfer.
source: since the IL-17-producing γδ T cell subsets cannot be reconstituted in adult animals by bone marrow transfer (Haas et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Haas et al., 2012.

claim: During embryonic development of certain γδ T cell subsets, the signaling threshold for activation of the TCR becomes markedly altered.
source: during embryonic development of certain γδ T cell subsets, the signaling threshold for activation of the TCR becomes markedly altered (Wencker et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wencker et al., 2013.

claim: Mature γδ T cells do not necessarily rely on a TCR stimulation as 'signal one', although they can still respond to that.
source: Hence, mature γδ T cells do not necessarily rely on a TCR stimulation as "'signal one"', although they can still respond to that (Strid et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Strid et al., 2011.

claim: Two members of the TNFR family, namely CD40 and RANK, have been implicated both in the development of DETCs and full maturation of mTECs.
source: Two members of the TNFR family, namely CD40 and RANK, have been implicated both in the development of DETCs and full maturation of mTECs (Hikosaka et al., 2008; Akiyama et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hikosaka et al., 2008; Akiyama et al., 2008.

claim: In the embryonic thymus, developing DETC precursors signal via the RANKL-RANK axis to immature mTECs, inducing their full maturation to Aire+ MHC-IIhigh mTECs.
source: and it seems that in the embryonic thymus, developing DETC precursors signal via the RANKL-RANK axis to immature mTECs, inducing their full maturation to Aire+ MHC-IIhigh mTECs (Roberts et al., 2012)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Roberts et al., 2012.

claim: Tnfrsf11a-/- mice have reduced numbers of DETCs.
source: Hence, Tnfrsf11a-/- mice have reduced numbers of DETCs.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: The instruction of γδ T cells is mediated by early or junctional TECs, or the timing of Ccl19-Cre-mediated recombination sharply coincides with the expression of the γδ T cell instructing program in TECs.
source: This would suggest that the instruction of γδ T cells is mediated by early or junctional TECs, or that the timing of Ccl19-Cre-mediated recombination sharply coincides with the expression of the γδ T cell instructing program in TECs.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the differential results between Ccl19-Cre and Foxn1-Cre experiments.

claim: Ccl19-Cre has been reported to target only maturing medullary thymic epithelial cells.
source: The latter has been reported to target only maturing medullary thymic epithelial cells (Onder et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Onder et al., 2015.

claim: NIK signaling in the early thymic stroma has a profound and long-lasting effect on the maturation and cytokine profile of developing γδ T cells.
source: Based on our observation that NIK signaling in the early thymic stroma has a profound and long-lasting effect on the maturation and cytokine profile of developing γδ T cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The impact of non-canonical signaling via NIK on the development of DETC precursors and IL-17-producing γδ T cells stems from signaling within the thymic stroma.
source: While our data does not exclude a role for canonical-NFκB signaling via RelA (Powolny-Budnicka et al., 2011), the impact of non-canonical signaling via NIK on the development of DETC precursors and IL-17-producing γδ T cells stems from signaling within the thymic stroma
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the conditional deletion experiments with citation acknowledging previous work.

claim: The conditional NIK mutant is a unique tool for further studies on thymic stroma influence on γδ T cell development.
source: for which the conditional NIK mutant is a unique tool for further studies
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the generated mouse model.

claim: Map3k14flox/wt animals were generated by gene targeting in embryonic stem (ES) cells, inserting LoxP sites up- and downstream of Exon 4 and 6 of the Map3k14 gene locus.
source: Map3k14flox/wt animals were generated by gene targeting in embryonic stem (ES) cells, thereby inserting LoxP sites up- and downstream of Exon 4 and 6 of the Map3k14 gene locus, respectively (Supp. Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the method used to generate the conditional mutant, with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: Map3k14flox/wt mice were crossed to a Deleter-Cre strain, followed by breeding the deleted locus to homozygosity.
source: These mice were first crossed to a Deleter-Cre strain, followed by breeding the deleted locus to homozygosity.
evidence: This describes the breeding strategy used.

claim: All animal experiments were approved by local authorities (Swiss cantonal veterinary office Zurich).
source: All animal experiments were approved by local authorities (Swiss cantonal veterinary office Zurich, KVET license numbers 86/2012, 70/2015, 100/2015 and 68/2013) and performed in strict accordance with the corresponding license.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval for the experiments.

claim: The ratio of Vγ4+ to Vγ6+ cells in the remaining fraction of IL-17-producing γδ T cells did not change in NIK-deficient mice.
source: The ratio of Vγ4+ to Vγ6+ cells in the remaining fraction of IL-17-producing γδ T cells did not change (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.
